questions.text: Let $f : \mathbf{R} \to \mathbf{R}$ be defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{2x^2-3x+2}{3x^2+x+3}$. Then $f$ is :
questions.sol:
$3x^2+x+3>0$ for all $x$, so $f$ is continuous on $\mathbf{R}$, and $f(x)\to\dfrac23$ as $x\to\infty$.
$f(0)=\dfrac23$, $f(1)=\dfrac17$: every value between $\dfrac17$ and $\dfrac23$ is taken once in $(0,1)$ and again in $(1,\infty)$, so $f$ is not one-one.
Range: $y(3x^2+x+3)=2x^2-3x+2 \Rightarrow (3y-2)x^2+(y+3)x+(3y-2)=0$; real $x$ needs $(y+3)^2\ge4(3y-2)^2$, a bounded interval of $y$.
So the range is a bounded interval, not $\mathbf{R}$: $f$ is not onto.
Hence $f$ is neither one-one nor onto.

questions.text: Consider the quadratic equation $(n^2-2n+2)x^2-3x+(n^2-2n+2)^2=0$, $n \in \mathbf{R}$. Let $\alpha$ be the minimum value of the product of its roots and $\beta$ be the maximum value of the sum of its roots. Then the sum of the first six terms of the G.P., whose first term is $\alpha$ and the common ratio is $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$, is :
questions.sol:
Let $m=n^2-2n+2=(n-1)^2+1\ge1$.
Product of roots $=\dfrac{m^2}{m}=m$, so $\alpha=1$ (at $n=1$).
Sum of roots $=\dfrac3m$, so $\beta=3$.
G.P.: first term $1$, ratio $\dfrac13$; $S_6=\dfrac{1-(1/3)^6}{1-1/3}=\dfrac{728}{729}\cdot\dfrac32=\dfrac{364}{243}$.

questions.text: Let $S=\left\{z \in \mathbb{C} : z^2+\sqrt6\,iz-3=0\right\}$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{z\in S} z^8$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$z=\dfrac{-\sqrt6 i\pm\sqrt{-6+12}}{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt6}{2}(\pm1-i)$.
Both roots have $|z|=\dfrac{\sqrt6}{2}\cdot\sqrt2=\sqrt3$, so $|z|^8=81$.
Arguments are $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and $-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$; multiplied by 8 they give $-2\pi$ and $-6\pi$, so $z^8=81$ for each root.
Sum $=81+81=162$.

questions.text:
The sum of all possible values of $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$, for which the system of equations :
$x\cos3\theta-8y-12z=0$
$x\cos2\theta+3y+3z=0$
$x+y+3z=0$
has a non-trivial solution, is equal to :
questions.sol:
Non-trivial solution $\iff \begin{vmatrix}\cos3\theta&-8&-12\\\cos2\theta&3&3\\1&1&3\end{vmatrix}=0$.
$6\cos3\theta+8(3\cos2\theta-3)-12(\cos2\theta-3)=6\cos3\theta+12\cos2\theta+12=0$.
With $c=\cos\theta$: $4c^3-3c+2(2c^2-1)+2=4c^3+4c^2-3c=c(2c-1)(2c+3)=0$.
$c=0$: $\theta=\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac{3\pi}2$; $c=\dfrac12$: $\theta=\dfrac\pi3,\dfrac{5\pi}3$ ($c=-\dfrac32$ impossible).
Sum $=2\pi+2\pi=4\pi$.

questions.text: A building has ground floor and 10 more floors. Nine persons enter in a lift at the ground floor. The lift goes up to the $10^{\text{th}}$ floor. The number of ways, in which any 4 persons exit at a floor and the remaining 5 persons exit at a different floor, if the lift does not stop at the first and the second floors, is equal to :
questions.sol:
Available floors: 3rd to 10th, i.e. 8 floors.
Choose the group of 4: $\binom94=126$ ways.
Floor for the group of 4 and a different floor for the group of 5: $8\times7=56$ ways.
Total $=126\times56=7056$.

questions.text: Let the mean and the variance of seven observations $2, 4, \alpha, 8, \beta, 12, 14$, $\alpha < \beta$, be 8 and 16 respectively. Then the quadratic equation whose roots are $3\alpha+2$ and $2\beta+1$ is :
questions.sol:
Mean: $40+\alpha+\beta=56 \Rightarrow \alpha+\beta=16$.
Variance: $\dfrac{\sum x^2}{7}-64=16 \Rightarrow \sum x^2=560$; $4+16+64+144+196=424$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=136$.
$\alpha\beta=\dfrac{256-136}{2}=60$, so $\alpha=6$, $\beta=10$.
Roots $3\alpha+2=20$ and $2\beta+1=21$: sum $41$, product $420$.
Equation: $x^2-41x+420=0$.

questions.text: A bag contains 6 blue and 6 green balls. Pairs of balls are drawn without replacement until the bag is empty. The probability that each drawn pair consists of one blue and one green ball is :
questions.sol:
Think of the 12 draws as a colour sequence; all $\binom{12}{6}=924$ placements of the blue balls are equally likely.
Each of the 6 pairs must be one blue and one green: in each pair the blue can be first or second, giving $2^6=64$ sequences.
Probability $=\dfrac{64}{924}=\dfrac{16}{231}$.

questions.text: Let C be a circle having centre in the first quadrant and touching the $x$-axis at a distance of 3 units from the origin. If the circle C has an intercept of length $6\sqrt3$ on $y$-axis, then the length of the chord of the circle C on the line $x-y=3$ is :
questions.sol:
Centre $(3, r)$, radius $r$.
$y$-intercept: $2\sqrt{r^2-9}=6\sqrt3 \Rightarrow r^2=36$, $r=6$; centre $(3,6)$.
Distance from centre to $x-y-3=0$: $\dfrac{|3-6-3|}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt2$.
Chord $=2\sqrt{36-18}=6\sqrt2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The eccentricity of an ellipse E with centre at the origin O is $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and its directrices are $x=\pm\dfrac{4\sqrt6}{3}$. Let $H : \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ be a hyperbola whose eccentricity is equal to the length of semi-major axis of E, and whose length of latus rectum is equal to the length of minor axis of E. Then the distance between the foci of H is :
questions.sol:
Ellipse: $\dfrac{A}{e}=\dfrac{4\sqrt6}{3} \Rightarrow A=\dfrac{4\sqrt6}{3}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=2\sqrt2$; $B^2=A^2(1-e^2)=2$, minor axis $=2\sqrt2$.
Hyperbola: $e_H=2\sqrt2 \Rightarrow b^2=a^2(e_H^2-1)=7a^2$.
Latus rectum $\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=14a=2\sqrt2 \Rightarrow a=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{7}$.
Distance between foci $=2ae_H=2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt2}{7}\cdot2\sqrt2=\dfrac87$.

questions.text: Let $x=9$ be a directrix of an ellipse E, whose centre is at the origin and eccentricity is $\dfrac13$. Let P $(\alpha, 0)$, $\alpha>0$, be a focus of E and AB be a chord passing through P. Then the locus of the mid point of AB is :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac ae=9$, $e=\dfrac13 \Rightarrow a=3$, $b^2=9\left(1-\dfrac19\right)=8$; focus P$(1,0)$.
Chord with mid point $(h,k)$: $\dfrac{hx}{9}+\dfrac{ky}{8}=\dfrac{h^2}{9}+\dfrac{k^2}{8}$.
It passes through $(1,0)$: $\dfrac h9=\dfrac{h^2}9+\dfrac{k^2}8 \Rightarrow 8h=8h^2+9k^2$.
Locus: $9y^2=8x(1-x)$.

questions.text: If $\sin\left(\tan^{-1}\left(x\sqrt2\right)\right)=\cot\left(\sin^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)$, $x\in(0,1)$, then the value of $x$ is :
questions.sol:
$\sin\left(\tan^{-1}x\sqrt2\right)=\dfrac{x\sqrt2}{\sqrt{1+2x^2}}$.
If $\sin\theta=\sqrt{1-x^2}$ ($\theta$ acute) then $\cos\theta=x$, so $\cot\theta=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.
$\dfrac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt{1+2x^2}}=\dfrac1{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \Rightarrow 2-2x^2=1+2x^2 \Rightarrow x^2=\dfrac14$.
$x=\dfrac12$.

questions.text: Let $\vec a=2\hat i+3\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\vec b=6\hat i+3\hat j+3\hat k$. Then the square of the area of the triangle with adjacent sides determined by the vectors $\left(2\vec a+3\vec b\right)$ and $\left(\vec a-\vec b\right)$ is :
questions.sol:
$(2\vec a+3\vec b)\times(\vec a-\vec b)=-2\,\vec a\times\vec b+3\,\vec b\times\vec a=-5\,\vec a\times\vec b$.
$\vec a\times\vec b=(9-9)\hat i-(6-18)\hat j+(6-18)\hat k=12\hat j-12\hat k$, $|\vec a\times\vec b|=12\sqrt2$.
Area $=\dfrac12\cdot5\cdot12\sqrt2=30\sqrt2$; square $=1800$.

questions.text: Let $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to2}\dfrac{(\tan(x-2))\left(rx^2+(p-2)x-2p\right)}{(x-2)^2}=5$ for some $r, p\in\mathbf{R}$. If the set of all possible values of $q$, such that the roots of the equation $rx^2-px+q=0$ lie in $(0,2)$, be the interval $(\alpha,\beta]$, then $4(\alpha+\beta)$ equals :
questions.sol:
Since $\dfrac{\tan(x-2)}{x-2}\to1$, we need $\dfrac{rx^2+(p-2)x-2p}{x-2}\to5$.
The numerator must vanish at $x=2$: $4r+2p-4-2p=0 \Rightarrow r=1$; then $x^2+(p-2)x-2p=(x-2)(x+p)$, so $2+p=5$, $p=3$.
$x^2-3x+q=0$ with both roots in $(0,2)$: $D\ge0 \Rightarrow q\le\dfrac94$; vertex $\dfrac32\in(0,2)$; $f(0)=q>0$; $f(2)=q-2>0$.
So $q\in\left(2,\dfrac94\right]$ and $4(\alpha+\beta)=4\left(2+\dfrac94\right)=17$.

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&3&-1\\2&1&\alpha\\0&1&-1\end{bmatrix}$ be a singular matrix. Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^x\left(t^2+2t+3\right)dt$, $x\in[1,\alpha]$. If M and m are respectively the maximum and the minimum values of $f$ in $[1,\alpha]$, then $3(M-m)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$|A|=1(-1-\alpha)-3(-2)+(-1)(2)=3-\alpha=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=3$.
$f'(x)=x^2+2x+3>0$, so $f$ is increasing: $M-m=f(3)-f(1)=\displaystyle\int_1^3(t^2+2t+3)\,dt$.
$=\left[\dfrac{t^3}{3}+t^2+3t\right]_1^3=27-\dfrac{13}{3}=\dfrac{68}{3}$.
$3(M-m)=68$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f : \mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be such that $f(xy)=f(x)f(y)$, for all $x, y\in\mathbf{R}$ and $f(0)\ne0$. Let $g : [1,\infty)\to\mathbf{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $$x^2g(x)=\int_1^x\left(t^2f(t)-tg(t)\right)dt.$$ Then $g(2)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$y=0$: $f(0)=f(x)f(0)$ and $f(0)\ne0$, so $f(x)=1$ for all $x$.
Differentiate: $2xg+x^2g'=x^2-xg \Rightarrow g'+\dfrac3xg=1$.
Integrating factor $x^3$: $(x^3g)'=x^3 \Rightarrow x^3g=\dfrac{x^4}{4}+C$.
$x=1$ in the given relation: $g(1)=0 \Rightarrow C=-\dfrac14$.
$g(2)=\dfrac{4-\frac14}{8}=\dfrac{15}{32}$.

questions.text: The area of the region $\{(x,y) : x^2-8x\le y\le-x\}$ is :
questions.sol:
Need $x^2-8x\le-x \Rightarrow x^2-7x\le0 \Rightarrow 0\le x\le7$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_0^7\left(-x-x^2+8x\right)dx=\int_0^7(7x-x^2)\,dx=\dfrac{343}{2}-\dfrac{343}{3}=\dfrac{343}{6}$.

questions.text: The value of the integral $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\left(\dfrac{x^3+|x|+1}{x^2+2|x|+1}\right)dx$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The part $\dfrac{x^3}{x^2+2|x|+1}$ is odd, so its integral is $0$.
The rest is even: $2\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{x+1}{(x+1)^2}\,dx=2\int_0^1\dfrac{dx}{x+1}=2\log_e2$.

questions.text: Let $R=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbf{N}\times\mathbf{N} : \log_e(x+y)\le2\right\}$. Then the minimum number of elements, required to be added in R to make it a transitive relation, is __________.
questions.sol:
$x+y\le e^2\approx7.39 \Rightarrow x+y\le7$; $R$ has $6+5+4+3+2+1=21$ pairs, all with $x,y\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$.
For any $a, c\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$: $(a,1)\in R$ and $(1,c)\in R$, so transitivity forces $(a,c)$.
So the smallest transitive relation containing $R$ is $\{1,\ldots,6\}^2$, with $36$ pairs (it is transitive).
Elements to add $=36-21=15$.

questions.text: Let the line $x-y=4$ intersect the circle C : $(x-4)^2+(y+3)^2=9$ at the points Q and R. If P$(\alpha,\beta)$ is a point on C such that PQ $=$ PR, then $(6\alpha+8\beta)^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
PQ $=$ PR puts P on the perpendicular bisector of QR, which is the line through the centre $(4,-3)$ perpendicular to $x-y=4$, i.e. along $(1,-1)$.
On C: P $=\left(4+s,\,-3-s\right)$ with $s=\pm\dfrac{3}{\sqrt2}$.
$6\alpha+8\beta=24+6s-24-8s=-2s$.
$(6\alpha+8\beta)^2=4s^2=4\cdot\dfrac92=18$.

questions.text: Let the image of the point P$(0,-5,0)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac y1=\dfrac{z+1}{-2}$ be the point R and the image of the point Q$\left(0,\dfrac{-1}{2},0\right)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-1}{-1}=\dfrac{y+9}{4}=\dfrac{z+1}{1}$ be the point S. Then the square of the area of the parallelogram PQRS is __________.
questions.sol:
Foot of P on the first line: $(1+2\lambda,\lambda,-1-2\lambda)$ with $(1+2\lambda,\lambda+5,-1-2\lambda)\cdot(2,1,-2)=0 \Rightarrow 9\lambda+9=0$, $\lambda=-1$: foot F $=(-1,-1,1)$, so R $=(-2,3,2)$.
Foot of Q on the second line: $(1-\mu,-9+4\mu,-1+\mu)$ with $\left(1-\mu,-\tfrac{17}{2}+4\mu,-1+\mu\right)\cdot(-1,4,1)=0 \Rightarrow 18\mu-36=0$, $\mu=2$: foot $(-1,-1,1)=$ F, so S $=\left(-2,-\tfrac32,2\right)$.
F is the mid point of both PR and QS, so PQRS is a parallelogram with diagonals $\vec{PR}=(-2,8,2)$, $\vec{QS}=(-2,-1,2)$.
$\vec{PR}\times\vec{QS}=(18,0,18)$, magnitude $18\sqrt2$; area $=\dfrac12\cdot18\sqrt2=9\sqrt2$.
Square of area $=162$.

questions.text:
Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^3+8\,; & x<0,\\ x^2-4\,; & x\ge0,\end{cases}$ and $g(x)=\begin{cases}(x-8)^{1/3}\,; & x<0,\\ (x+4)^{1/2}\,; & x\ge0.\end{cases}$
Then the number of points, where the function $gof$ is discontinuous, is __________.
questions.sol:
$g$ is continuous except at $0$: $g(0^-)=(-8)^{1/3}=-2$, $g(0)=2$. $f$ is continuous except at $0$: $f(0^-)=8$, $f(0)=-4$.
So $g\circ f$ can fail only where $f$ crosses $0$ or at $x=0$.
$x=-2$: $f$ changes sign, $g\circ f$ jumps between $-2$ and $2$ → discontinuous.
$x=2$: $f=x^2-4$ changes sign → discontinuous.
$x=0$: $g(f(0^-))=g(8)=\sqrt{12}$, $g(f(0))=g(-4)=(-12)^{1/3}$ → discontinuous.
Number of points $=3$.

questions.text: The percentage error in the calculated volume of a sphere, if there is 2% error in its diameter measurement, is _________.
questions.sol:
$V=\dfrac{\pi D^3}{6} \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=3\,\dfrac{\Delta D}{D}$.
Percentage error $=3\times2\%=6\%$.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List-IList-II
A. Boltzmann constantI. $[\mathrm{M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}}]$
B. Stefan's constantII. $[\mathrm{ML^2T^{-1}}]$
C. Planck's constantIII. $[\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}}]$
D. Gravitational constantIV. $[\mathrm{ML^0T^{-3}K^{-4}}]$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Boltzmann constant $k=\dfrac{E}{T}$: $[\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}}]$ → III.
Stefan's constant $\sigma=\dfrac{E}{At\,T^4}$: $[\mathrm{MT^{-3}K^{-4}}]$ → IV.
Planck's constant $h=\dfrac{E}{\nu}$: $[\mathrm{ML^2T^{-1}}]$ → II.
Gravitational constant $G=\dfrac{Fr^2}{m^2}$: $[\mathrm{M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}}]$ → I.
So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.text: A solid sphere $(A)$ of mass $5m$ and a spherical shell $(B)$ of mass $m$, both having same radius, are placed on a rough surface. When a force of same magnitude is applied tangentially at the highest points of $A$ and $B$, they start rolling without slipping with an acceleration of $a_A$ and $a_B$, respectively. The ratio of $a_A$ and $a_B$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Let $I=kMR^2$ and friction $f$ act forwards: $F+f=Ma$, $(F-f)R=kMR^2\cdot\dfrac aR$.
Adding: $2F=Ma(1+k) \Rightarrow a=\dfrac{2F}{M(1+k)}$.
Solid sphere ($M=5m$, $k=\tfrac25$): $a_A=\dfrac{2F}{7m}$.
Shell ($M=m$, $k=\tfrac23$): $a_B=\dfrac{6F}{5m}$.
$\dfrac{a_A}{a_B}=\dfrac{2}{7}\cdot\dfrac56=\dfrac{5}{21}$.

questions.text: A body of mass 1 kg moves along a straight line with a velocity $v=2x^2$. The work done by the body during displacement from $x=0$ to 5 m is _________ J.
questions.sol:
At $x=0$, $v=0$; at $x=5$ m, $v=2(25)=50$ m/s.
By the work-energy theorem, $W=\Delta K=\dfrac12(1)(50)^2-0=1250$ J.

questions.text: A cylinder with adiabatic walls is closed at both ends and is divided into two compartments by a frictionless adiabatic piston. Ideal gas is filled in both (left and right) the compartments at same $P$, $V$, $T$. Heating is started from left side until pressure changes to $\dfrac{27P}{8}$. If initial volume of each compartment was 9 litres then the final volume in right-hand side compartment is ________ litres. (for this ideal gas $C_P/C_V=1.5$)
questions.sol:
The gas on the right is compressed slowly and adiabatically, and its final pressure equals the left side's, $\dfrac{27P}{8}$.
$PV^{\gamma}=$ constant: $V_2=9\left(\dfrac{8}{27}\right)^{1/1.5}=9\left(\dfrac{8}{27}\right)^{2/3}=9\cdot\dfrac49=4$ litres.

questions.text: For an electromagnetic wave propagating through vacuum, $\vec k$, $\vec E$ and $\omega$ represent propagation vector, electric field and angular frequency, respectively. The magnetic field associated with this wave is represented by :
questions.sol:
$\vec E$, $\vec B$, $\vec k$ form a right-handed set with $\vec E\times\vec B$ along $\vec k$, so $\vec B$ is along $\vec k\times\vec E$.
Magnitude: $B=\dfrac Ec=\dfrac{kE}{\omega}$ since $c=\dfrac\omega k$.
Hence $\vec B=\dfrac{\vec k\times\vec E}{\omega}$.

questions.text: Two identical bodies A and B of equal masses have initial velocities $\vec v_1=4\hat i$ m/s and $\vec v_2=4\hat j$ m/s respectively. The body A has acceleration $\vec a_1=6\hat i+6\hat j$ m/s$^2$ while the acceleration of the other body B is zero. The centre of mass of the two bodies moves in __________ path.
questions.sol:
$\vec v_{cm}=\dfrac{\vec v_1+\vec v_2}{2}=2\hat i+2\hat j$, $\vec a_{cm}=\dfrac{\vec a_1+\vec 0}{2}=3\hat i+3\hat j$.
The acceleration is parallel to the initial velocity, so the centre of mass moves in a straight line.

questions.text: Figure represents the extension $(\Delta l)$ of a wire of length 1 meter, suspended from the ceiling of the room at one end with a load $W$ connected to the other end. If the cross-sectional area of the wire is $10^{-5}$ m$^2$ then the Young's modulus of the wire is _________ N/m$^2$.
questions.sol:
From the graph, $W=10$ N gives $\Delta l=1\times10^{-4}$ m.
$Y=\dfrac{W/A}{\Delta l/L}=\dfrac{10/10^{-5}}{10^{-4}/1}=\dfrac{10^6}{10^{-4}}=1.0\times10^{10}$ N/m$^2$.

questions.text: A cylindrical vessel of 40 cm radius is completely filled with water and its capacity is 528 dm$^3$ (dm : decimeter) The vessel is placed on a solid block of exactly same height as vessel. If a small hole is made at 70 cm below the top of water level, then horizontal range of water falling on the ground in the beginning is ________ cm.
questions.sol:
Height of vessel: $\pi r^2h=528000$ cm$^3$ $\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{528000\times7}{22\times1600}=105$ cm.
Efflux speed $v=\sqrt{2g(70\text{ cm})}$; the hole is $105-70+105=140$ cm above the ground.
Range $=v\sqrt{\dfrac{2H}{g}}=2\sqrt{70\times140}=2\times70\sqrt2=140\sqrt2$ cm.

questions.text: If 2 mole of an ideal monoatomic gas at temperature $T$, is mixed with 6 mole of another ideal monoatomic gas at temperature $2T$ then the temperature of mixture is :
questions.sol:
Internal energy is conserved and both gases have $C_V=\dfrac32R$.
$2T+6(2T)=8T_{mix} \Rightarrow T_{mix}=\dfrac{14T}{8}=\dfrac74T$.

questions.text: A spring stretches by 2 mm when it is loaded with a mass of 200 g. From equilibrium position the mass is further pulled down by 2 mm and released. The frequency associated with the system and maxmimum energy in the spring are __________ Hz and _________ J, respectively. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
$k=\dfrac{mg}{x}=\dfrac{0.2\times10}{0.002}=1000$ N/m.
$\omega=\sqrt{\dfrac km}=\sqrt{5000}=10\sqrt{50}$ rad/s, so $f=\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}=\dfrac{5\sqrt{50}}{\pi}$ Hz.
Maximum extension $=2+2=4$ mm, so maximum spring energy $=\dfrac12(1000)(0.004)^2=8\times10^{-3}$ J.

questions.text: The electric potential as a function of $x$, $y$ is given by $V=5(x^2-y^2)$ V. The electric field at a point $(2,3)$ m is __________ V/m.
questions.sol:
$\vec E=-\nabla V=-10x\,\hat i+10y\,\hat j$.
At $(2,3)$: $\vec E=-20\hat i+30\hat j$ V/m.

questions.text: A current of 30 A each flows in opposite directions in two conducting wires, placed parallel to each other at a distance of 8 cm. The magnetic field at the mid point between the two wires is ______ $\mu$T. $\left(\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}=10^{-7}\text{ N/A}^2\right)$
questions.sol:
Each wire at $d=4$ cm: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi d}=\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times30}{0.04}=1.5\times10^{-4}$ T.
For opposite currents the fields at the mid point are in the same direction and add.
$B=3\times10^{-4}$ T $=300\ \mu$T.

questions.text: A square loop of side 2 cm is placed in a time varying magnetic field with magnitude as $B=0.4\sin(300t)$ Tesla. The normal to the plane of loop makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the field. The maximum induced emf produced in the loop is ___________ mV.
questions.sol:
$\phi=BA\cos60^\circ=0.4\sin(300t)\times(4\times10^{-4})\times\dfrac12$.
$\varepsilon_{max}=0.4\times300\times4\times10^{-4}\times\dfrac12=0.024$ V $=24$ mV.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A sphere of capacitance 100 pF is charged to a potential of 100 V. Another identical uncharged metal sphere is brought in contact with the charged sphere, then the change in the total energy stored on these spheres, when they touch is $\alpha\times10^{-7}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is __________. (combined capacitance of spheres is 200 pF)
questions.sol:
Initial: $U_1=\dfrac12CV^2=\dfrac12(10^{-10})(10^4)=5\times10^{-7}$ J, charge $Q=10^{-8}$ C.
Final: $U_2=\dfrac{Q^2}{2C'}=\dfrac{10^{-16}}{4\times10^{-10}}=2.5\times10^{-7}$ J.
Change $=2.5\times10^{-7}$ J, so $\alpha=\dfrac52$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The energy released if hydrogen atoms are combined to form $_2^4\mathrm{He}$ is ________ MeV. (Take binding energies per nucleon of $_1^2\mathrm{H}$ and $_2^4\mathrm{He}$ as 1.1 MeV and 7.2 MeV, respectively)
questions.sol:
$2\,{}_1^2\mathrm H\to{}_2^4\mathrm{He}$.
Binding energy of He $=4\times7.2=28.8$ MeV; of two deuterons $=2\times2\times1.1=4.4$ MeV.
Energy released $=28.8-4.4=24.4$ MeV.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Angle of minimum deviation is equal to the half of the angle of prism in an equilateral prism. The refractive index of the prism is _________.
questions.sol:
$A=60^\circ$, $\delta_m=30^\circ$.
$\mu=\dfrac{\sin\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}}{\sin\frac A2}=\dfrac{\sin45^\circ}{\sin30^\circ}=\sqrt2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Refer to the logic circuit given below. For two inputs $(A=1, B=1)$ and $(A=0, B=1)$, output (Y) will be __________.
questions.sol:
The OR gate gets $\bar A$ and $B$; the AND gate gets $\bar A$ and $B$; both feed a NOR gate.
$Y=\overline{(\bar A+B)+\bar AB}=\overline{\bar A+B}=A\bar B$.
$A=1,B=1$: $Y=0$. $A=0,B=1$: $Y=0$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The velocity at which 6 kg mass (shown in figure) strikes the ground when it is released from a height of 6 m above the ground is _________ m/s. Assume pulley is massless and string is light and inextensible. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
$a=\dfrac{(6-2)g}{6+2}=5$ m/s$^2$.
$v=\sqrt{2as}=\sqrt{2\times5\times6}=\sqrt{60}\approx7.74$ m/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a Young double slit experiment, the wavelength of incident light is 6000 Å, the separation between slits $S_1$ and $S_2$ is 5 cm and the distance between slits plane and screen is 50 cm, as shown in the figure below. If the resultant intensity at $P$ is equal to the intensity due to individual slits, the path difference between interfering waves is _________ Å.
questions.note: Official final key: options (1) and (3) are both accepted.
questions.sol:
$I=4I_0\cos^2\dfrac\phi2=I_0 \Rightarrow \cos\dfrac\phi2=\pm\dfrac12 \Rightarrow \phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ or $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ (within one wavelength).
Path difference $=\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi}\phi=\dfrac\lambda3=2000$ Å or $\dfrac{2\lambda}{3}=4000$ Å.
Both values are listed, and the official key accepts both options.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A block takes $t$ time to slide down a plane inclined at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal. If the surface is made smooth (frictionless), the block takes time $\dfrac t2$ to slide down the plane. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inclined plane is $\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{100}\right)$. The value of $\alpha$ is _________.
questions.sol:
For the same distance from rest, $t\propto\dfrac1{\sqrt a}$, so $a_{rough}=\dfrac{a_{smooth}}{4}$.
$g(\sin45^\circ-\mu\cos45^\circ)=\dfrac{g\sin45^\circ}{4} \Rightarrow 1-\mu=\dfrac14$.
$\mu=0.75=\dfrac{75}{100}$, so $\alpha=75$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The de Broglie wavelength for an electron accelerated through the potential difference of $V_1$ volt is $\lambda_1$. When the potential difference is changed to $V_2$ volt, the associated de Broglie wavelength is increased by 50%. If $(V_1/V_2)=(9/\alpha)$, then the value of $\alpha$ is _________.
questions.sol:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}\propto\dfrac1{\sqrt V}$.
$\lambda_2=1.5\lambda_1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{V_1}{V_2}=(1.5)^2=\dfrac94$.
$\alpha=4$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: A moving coil of galvanometer when shunted with 2 $\Omega$ resistance gives a full scale deflection for a current of 500 mA. When a resistance of 470 $\Omega$ is connected in series it gives a full scale deflection for 10 V potential applied on it. The value of resistance of galvanometer coil is _________ $\Omega$.
questions.sol:
Shunt: $I_gG=(0.5-I_g)\times2 \Rightarrow I_g(G+2)=1$.
Series: $I_g(G+470)=10$.
Dividing: $\dfrac{G+470}{G+2}=10 \Rightarrow 9G=450 \Rightarrow G=50\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two cells of emfs 1 V and 2 V and internal resistance 2 $\Omega$ and 1 $\Omega$, respectively connected in parallel, gave a current of 1 A through an external resistance. If the polarity of one cell is reversed, then value of current through the external resistance will be $\dfrac{\alpha}{5}$ A. The value of $\alpha$ is _________.
questions.sol:
Parallel combination: $r_{eq}=\dfrac{2\times1}{3}=\dfrac23\ \Omega$, $E_{eq}=\dfrac{\frac12+\frac21}{\frac12+1}=\dfrac53$ V.
$1=\dfrac{5/3}{R+2/3} \Rightarrow R=1\ \Omega$.
Reversing the 1 V cell: $E_{eq}=\dfrac{-\frac12+2}{\frac32}=1$ V.
$I=\dfrac{1}{1+\frac23}=\dfrac35$ A, so $\alpha=3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms an image which is double the size of object when the object is placed at two different positions. The distance between the two positions of the object is __________ cm.
questions.sol:
$m=\dfrac{f}{f-u}$ with $f=-10$ cm.
Real image, $m=-2$: $\dfrac{-10}{-10-u}=-2 \Rightarrow u=-15$ cm.
Virtual image, $m=+2$: $\dfrac{-10}{-10-u}=2 \Rightarrow u=-5$ cm.
Distance between the positions $=15-5=10$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Which of the following contain the same number of atoms ?
(Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of H, He, O and S are 1, 4, 16 and 32 respectively)
A. 2 g of $\mathrm{O_2}$ gas
B. 4 g of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ gas
C. 1400 mL of $\mathrm{O_2}$ at STP
D. 0.05 L of He at STP
E. 0.0625 mol of $\mathrm{H_2}$ gas
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: $\dfrac{2}{32}=\dfrac1{16}$ mol $\mathrm{O_2}$ → $\dfrac18$ mol atoms.
B: $\dfrac4{64}=\dfrac1{16}$ mol $\mathrm{SO_2}$ → $\dfrac3{16}$ mol atoms.
C: $\dfrac{1.4}{22.4}=\dfrac1{16}$ mol $\mathrm{O_2}$ → $\dfrac18$ mol atoms.
D: $\dfrac{0.05}{22.4}\approx0.0022$ mol atoms.
E: $0.0625=\dfrac1{16}$ mol $\mathrm{H_2}$ → $\dfrac18$ mol atoms.
A, C and E have the same number of atoms.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The Bohr radius of a hydrogen like species is 70.53 pm. The species and the stationary state (n) are respectively
(Given : Hydrogen atom Bohr radius is 52.9 pm)
questions.sol:
$r_n=52.9\,\dfrac{n^2}{Z}$ pm.
$\dfrac{n^2}{Z}=\dfrac{70.53}{52.9}=\dfrac43$, so $n=2$, $Z=3$.
The species is $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ in $n=2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The number of compounds among $\mathrm{SO_2}$, $\mathrm{SO_3}$, $\mathrm{SF_4}$, $\mathrm{SF_6}$ and $\mathrm{H_2S}$ in which sulphur does not obey the Octet rule is 3.
Statement II : Among $[\mathrm{H_2O, ClF_3, SF_4}]$, $[\mathrm{NH_3, BrF_5, SF_4}]$, $[\mathrm{BrF_5, ClF_3, XeF_4}]$ and $[\mathrm{XeF_4, ClF_3, H_2O}]$, the number of sets in which all the molecules have one lone pair of electrons on the central atom is 1.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: S has an expanded octet in $\mathrm{SO_2}$ (10 e$^-$), $\mathrm{SO_3}$ (12), $\mathrm{SF_4}$ (10) and $\mathrm{SF_6}$ (12); only $\mathrm{H_2S}$ obeys the octet. That is 4 compounds, so Statement I is false.
Lone pairs on the central atom: $\mathrm{H_2O}$ 2, $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ 2, $\mathrm{SF_4}$ 1, $\mathrm{NH_3}$ 1, $\mathrm{BrF_5}$ 1, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ 2.
Only the set $[\mathrm{NH_3, BrF_5, SF_4}]$ has one lone pair on every central atom, so Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
Given $\mathrm{V_1}$ and $\mathrm{V_2}$ are initial and final volumes respectively.
List-I (Isothermal process)List-II (Expression)
A. Reversible expansionI. $q=0$
B. Free expansionII. $q=nRT\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}$
C. Irreversible CompressionIII. $w=-p_{ext}(V_1-V_2)$
D. Cyclic reversibleIV. $\dfrac{q_{rev}}{T}=0$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A. Isothermal reversible expansion: $\Delta U=0$, $q=-w=nRT\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}$ → II.
B. Free expansion of an ideal gas: $w=0$ and $\Delta U=0$, so $q=0$ → I.
C. Irreversible compression against a constant external pressure: work given by the $p_{ext}$ expression → III.
D. Cyclic reversible process: entropy is a state function, so $\oint\dfrac{q_{rev}}{T}=0$ → IV.
So A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
(Chamber 1: 18 g glucose in 100 mL aqueous solution; Chamber 2: 30 g glucose in 250 mL aqueous solution; the chambers are separated by a semi-permeable membrane.)
Statement I : $\mathrm{H_2O}$ molecules move from the chamber 1 to chamber 2.
Statement II : The osmotic pressure of a solution prepared by dissolving 50 mg of potassium sulphate (molar mass $=174$ g/mol) in 2 L of water (at 27 °C) is 0.0107 bar. (Given: $R=0.083$ dm$^3$ bar K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ and assume complete dissociation of electrolyte)
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Chamber 1: $\dfrac{18}{180}=0.1$ mol in 0.1 L → 1 M. Chamber 2: $\dfrac{30}{180}=\dfrac16$ mol in 0.25 L → 0.667 M.
Water moves by osmosis from the dilute side (chamber 2) to the concentrated side (chamber 1), so Statement I is false.
$\mathrm{K_2SO_4}$: $i=3$, $C=\dfrac{0.05/174}{2}=1.437\times10^{-4}$ M.
$\pi=iCRT=3\times1.437\times10^{-4}\times0.083\times300\approx0.0107$ bar, so Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Given is a concentrated solution of a weak electrolyte $\mathrm{A_xB_y}$ of concentration '$c$' and dissociation constant '$K$'. The degree of dissociation is given by :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{A_xB_y}\rightleftharpoons x\mathrm A^{y+}+y\mathrm B^{x-}$: at equilibrium $c(1-\alpha)$, $xc\alpha$, $yc\alpha$.
$K=\dfrac{(xc\alpha)^x(yc\alpha)^y}{c(1-\alpha)}\approx x^xy^y\,c^{x+y-1}\alpha^{x+y}$ for a weak electrolyte ($1-\alpha\approx1$).
$\alpha=\left(\dfrac{K}{c^{x+y-1}x^xy^y}\right)^{\frac1{x+y}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For a general redox reaction
Anode: $\mathrm{Red_1\to Ox_1^{n_1+}+n_1e^-}$
Cathode: $\mathrm{Ox_2+n_2e^-\to Red_2^{n_2-}}$
Which of the following statement is incorrect ?
options: The overall reaction can be written as $\mathrm{n_2Red_1+n_1Ox_2\rightleftharpoons n_2Ox_1^{n_1+}+n_1Red_2^{n_2-}}$
The electrons do not appear in the overall reaction because electrons produced at the anode are consumed at the cathode.
If the reaction is carried out reversibly, the electrical work done is equal to the ratio of charge and potential difference through which charge is moved.
questions.sol:
(1) Multiplying the anode reaction by $n_2$ and the cathode reaction by $n_1$ balances the electrons: correct.
(2) Electrons released at the anode are consumed at the cathode: correct.
(3) Nernst: $\dfrac{E-E^\circ}{RT/F}=-\dfrac{2.303}{n}\log_{10}Q$, a straight line through the origin with slope proportional to $\dfrac1n$: correct.
(4) Reversible electrical work $=$ charge $\times$ potential difference ($w=-nFE$), not their ratio: incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In a period, the first ionisation enthalpy of the element at extreme left and the negative electron gain enthalpy of the extreme right element, except noble gases, are respectively.
questions.sol:
Across a period, ionisation enthalpy increases, so the alkali metal at the extreme left has the lowest first ionisation enthalpy.
The halogen at the extreme right (noble gases excluded) has the most negative electron gain enthalpy, i.e. the highest negative electron gain enthalpy.
So: lowest and highest.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : $\mathrm{F_2O < H_2O < Cl_2O}$ is the correct trend in terms of bond angle.
Statement II : $\mathrm{SiF_4}$, $\mathrm{SnF_4}$ and $\mathrm{PbF_4}$ are ionic in nature.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Bond angles: $\mathrm{F_2O}\approx103^\circ$ (bond pairs drawn towards F), $\mathrm{H_2O}\approx104.5^\circ$, $\mathrm{Cl_2O}\approx111^\circ$ (bulky Cl atoms). Statement I is true.
$\mathrm{SnF_4}$ and $\mathrm{PbF_4}$ are ionic, but $\mathrm{SiF_4}$ is a covalent molecule (a gas). Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The correct order of first $(\Delta_iH_1)$ and second $(\Delta_iH_2)$ ionisation enthalpy values of Cr and Mn are :
A. $\Delta_iH_1$ : Cr $>$ Mn
B. $\Delta_iH_2$ : Cr $>$ Mn
C. $\Delta_iH_1$ : Mn $>$ Cr
D. $\Delta_iH_2$ : Mn $>$ Cr
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
First ionisation: Mn ($3d^54s^2$, 717 kJ mol$^{-1}$) $>$ Cr ($3d^54s^1$, 653 kJ mol$^{-1}$), so C is correct.
Second ionisation: $\mathrm{Cr^+}$ is $3d^5$ (stable half-filled), so Cr (1592) $>$ Mn (1509), so B is correct.
Answer: B and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following sequences of hybridisation, geometry and magnetic nature are correct for the given coordination compounds ?
A. $[\mathrm{NiCl_4}]^{2-}$ – $sp^3$, tetrahedral, paramagnetic
B. $[\mathrm{Ni(NH_3)_6}]^{2+}$ – $sp^3d^2$, octahedral, paramagnetic
C. $[\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}]$ – $sp^3$, tetrahedral, paramagnetic
D. $[\mathrm{Ni(CN)_4}]^{2-}$ – $dsp^2$, square planar, diamagnetic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A. $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ ($3d^8$) with weak-field $\mathrm{Cl^-}$: $sp^3$, tetrahedral, 2 unpaired electrons → correct.
B. $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ with six $\mathrm{NH_3}$: outer orbital $sp^3d^2$, octahedral, 2 unpaired → correct.
C. Ni(0) in $[\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}]$: $3d^{10}$, $sp^3$ tetrahedral, but diamagnetic → incorrect.
D. $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ with strong-field $\mathrm{CN^-}$: $dsp^2$, square planar, diamagnetic → correct.
Answer: A, B and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A mixture of $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$ (sugar) and NaCl can be separated by dissolving sugar in alcohol, due to differential solubility.
Statement II : Rose essence from rose petals is seperated by steam distillation due to its high volatility and insolubility in $\mathrm{H_2O}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: sugar dissolves in alcohol while NaCl does not, so the mixture can be separated by differential solubility (true).
Statement II: essential oils such as rose essence are steam volatile and immiscible with water, so they are isolated by steam distillation (true).
Both statements are true.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: Shown below is the structure of methyl acetate with three different $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ carbon - oxygen bonds. The correct order of bond lengths of these bonds is :
questions.sol:
$\alpha$ is the C=O double bond: shortest.
$\beta$ (acyl C–O) gains partial double bond character by resonance of the O lone pair with C=O: $\mathrm{CH_3C(=O)-OCH_3 \leftrightarrow CH_3C(-O^-)=O^+CH_3}$.
$\gamma$ ($\mathrm{O-CH_3}$) is a pure single bond: longest.
Order: $\alpha<\beta<\gamma$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: '$x$' is the product which is obtained by the hydrolysis of prop-1-yne in the presence of mercuric sulphate under dilute acidic medium at 333 K. '$y$' is the product which is obtained by the reaction of ethane nitrile with methyl magnesium bromide in dry ether followed by hydrolysis. IUPAC name of product obtained from '$x$' and '$y$' in the presence of barium hydroxide followed by heating is :
questions.sol:
$x$: $\mathrm{CH_3C{\equiv}CH}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H^+}}\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$ (acetone).
$y$: $\mathrm{CH_3CN+CH_3MgBr}$, then hydrolysis → $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$ (acetone).
$\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$: aldol condensation gives $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2COCH_3}$; heating dehydrates it to $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CHCOCH_3}$.
IUPAC name: 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: An optically active alkyl bromide $\mathrm{C_4H_9Br}$, reacts with ethanolic KOH to form major compound [A] which reacts with bromine to give compound [B]. Compound [B] reacts with ethanolic KOH and sodamide to give compound [C]. One molecule of water adds to compound [C] on warming with mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid at 333 K to form compound [D]. The functional group in compound D will be confirmed by :
questions.sol:
The optically active $\mathrm{C_4H_9Br}$ is 2-bromobutane.
Ethanolic KOH → but-2-ene [A] (Saytzeff); $\mathrm{Br_2}$ → 2,3-dibromobutane [B].
Ethanolic KOH then $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$ → but-2-yne [C].
$\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H_2SO_4}$ hydration → butan-2-one [D], $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH_3}$.
A methyl ketone is confirmed by the haloform test.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction (benzyl phenyl ether with HI).
Statement I : In the above reaction, product formed will be a mixture of benzyl alcohol and iodobenzene.
Statement II : In the above reaction, the $-\mathrm{O-CH_2}-$ bond is cleaved to give the product.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
The O–aryl bond has partial double bond character and the phenyl carbon does not undergo $S_N$ attack.
After protonation, $\mathrm{I^-}$ attacks the benzylic $\mathrm{CH_2}$, so the $\mathrm{O-CH_2}$ bond is cleaved: Statement II is true.
Products: phenol and benzyl iodide, not benzyl alcohol and iodobenzene: Statement I is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following organic reaction sequence. Choose the final product (X) from the following (consider the major product in all intermediate reactions)
Propanoic acid: (i) $\mathrm{NH_3/\Delta}$ (ii) $\mathrm{NaOH/Br_2}$ (iii) $\mathrm{HNO_2/H_2O}$, 0°C (iv) $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl}$, 0°C → (X) Major Product
questions.sol:
(i) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH+NH_3}$, heat → $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2}$.
(ii) Hofmann bromamide degradation → $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$.
(iii) $\mathrm{HNO_2}$: the aliphatic diazonium salt decomposes to ethanol, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$.
(iv) Ethanol reduces benzenediazonium chloride: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl+CH_3CH_2OH\to C_6H_6+N_2+CH_3CHO+HCl}$.
X is benzene.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The number of compounds from the following which can undergo reaction with $\mathrm{Br_2}$/KOH (alcoholic) to give respective products and these respective products can also be obtained separately by Gabriel phthalimide reaction is :
questions.sol:
Hofmann bromamide degradation needs a primary amide ($\mathrm{-CONH_2}$); the N-substituted amides $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CONHCH_2CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CCONHCH_3}$ do not react.
$\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2}\to\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$: aniline cannot be made by the Gabriel synthesis (aryl halides do not react).
$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CONH_2}\to\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2}$, $\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2}\to\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$, $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CONH_2}\to\mathrm{C_6H_{11}NH_2}$: primary alkyl amines, also obtainable by Gabriel synthesis.
Number $=3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reactions. Total number of electrons in the $\pi$ bonds and lone pair of electrons in the product (X) is :
$\mathrm{CHO{-}(CHOH)_4{-}CH_2OH}$: (i) HI, $\Delta$ (ii) $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$/10-20 atm/773 K (iii) Benzoyl chloride/Anhyd. $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ → (X) Major product
questions.sol:
(i) Glucose with HI on prolonged heating → n-hexane.
(ii) $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$, 773 K, 10–20 atm: aromatisation of n-hexane → benzene.
(iii) Friedel–Crafts benzoylation → benzophenone, $\mathrm{C_6H_5COC_6H_5}$ (X).
$\pi$ electrons: two rings $2\times6=12$, plus C=O $2$ → $14$; lone pairs on O: $2$ pairs $=4$ electrons.
Total $=18$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Treatment of a gas 'X' with a freshly prepared ferrous sulphate solution gives a compound 'Y' as a brown ring. The compounds X and Y are.
questions.sol:
Nitric oxide combines with freshly prepared $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$: $\mathrm{FeSO_4+NO\to[Fe(NO)]SO_4}$ (brown), the brown ring test.
X $=$ NO, Y $=[\mathrm{Fe(NO)}]\mathrm{SO_4}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: An excess of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ is added to 100 mL of a 0.05 M solution of tetraaquadichloridochromium (III) chloride. The number of moles of AgCl precipitated will be __________ $\times10^{-3}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
$[\mathrm{Cr(H_2O)_4Cl_2}]\mathrm{Cl}$ has one ionisable chloride per formula unit.
Moles of complex $=0.1\times0.05=5\times10^{-3}$, so AgCl $=5\times10^{-3}$ mol.
Answer: 5.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: An alkane (Y) requires 8 moles of oxygen for complete combustion and on chlorination with $\mathrm{Cl_2}/h\nu$, (Y) gives only one monochlorinated product (Z). The total number of primary carbon atoms in (Y) is __________.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}+\dfrac{3n+1}{2}O_2}$: $\dfrac{3n+1}{2}=8 \Rightarrow n=5$.
The $\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$ isomer giving only one monochloro product is neopentane, $\mathrm{C(CH_3)_4}$.
It has 4 primary carbon atoms.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: 500 mL of 0.2 M $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ solution in basic medium when mixed with 500 mL of 1.5 M KI solution, oxidises iodide ions to liberate molecular iodine. This liberated iodine is then titrated with a standard $x$ M thiosulphate solution in presence of starch till the end point. If 300 mL of thiosulphate was consumed, then the value of $x$ is __________.
questions.sol:
In basic medium $\mathrm{MnO_4^-\to MnO_2}$ (3 electrons): $\mathrm{2MnO_4^-+6I^-+4H_2O\to2MnO_2+3I_2+8OH^-}$.
$\mathrm{MnO_4^-}=0.1$ mol (iodide, 0.75 mol, is in excess), so $\mathrm{I_2}=0.15$ mol.
$\mathrm{I_2+2S_2O_3^{2-}\to2I^-+S_4O_6^{2-}}$: thiosulphate $=0.3$ mol.
$x=\dfrac{0.3}{0.3}=1$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In a closed flask at 600 K, one mole of $\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g)}$ attains equilibrium as given below :
$$\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g)\rightleftharpoons2XY_2(g)}$$At equilibrium, 75% $\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g)}$ was dissociated and the total pressure is 1 atm. The magnitude of $\Delta_rG^\ominus$ (in kJ mol$^{-1}$) at this temperature is _________. (Nearest Integer)
(Given : $R=8.3$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$; $\ln10=2.3$, $\log2=0.3$, $\log3=0.48$, $\log5=0.69$, $\log7=0.84$)
questions.sol:
At equilibrium: $\mathrm{X_2Y_4}=0.25$ mol, $\mathrm{XY_2}=1.5$ mol, total $1.75$ mol, $P=1$ atm.
$K_p=\dfrac{(1.5/1.75)^2}{0.25/1.75}=\dfrac{2.25}{0.4375}=\dfrac{36}{7}$.
$\log K_p=2(0.3+0.48)-0.84=0.72$.
$\Delta_rG^\ominus=-2.3RT\log K_p=-2.3\times8.3\times600\times0.72\approx-8247$ J mol$^{-1}$.
Magnitude $\approx8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.text:
Decomposition of a hydrocarbon follows the equation $k=\left(5.5\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\right)e^{-28000\,\mathrm K/T}$. The activation energy of reaction is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
Given : $R=8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$
questions.sol:
Comparing with $k=Ae^{-E_a/RT}$: $\dfrac{E_a}{R}=28000$ K.
$E_a=28000\times8.3=232400$ J mol$^{-1}\approx232$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
